problem:
The value $V=V(t)$ of a certain art object $t$ years after its production can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=kV
$$

where $k>0$ is the growth rate. If it was initially worth $$2\,000,$ and $V(10)=10\,000$, calculate the value  of the growth rate $k$ to the nearest percent.

feedback.problem:
The population of a bacterial culture $N=N(t)$ after $t$ hours can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=kN,
$$

where $k>0$ is the growth rate. If the culture initially contained $500$ bacteria, and $N(3)=2\,000,$ calculate the growth rate $k$ to the nearest percent.
feedback.worked_solution:
We model the population of the bacterial culture using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=kN.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
N(t)={N}_{0}\,{e}^{kt},
$$

where ${N}_{0}$ is the initial population.

We're told that the culture initially contained $500$ bacteria, so we have ${N}_{0}=500.$

Therefore, the population $N$ at time $t$ is

$$
N(t)=500\,{e}^{kt}.
$$

Finally, to find the value of $k,$ we substitute $N(3)=2\,000$ into the equation above and solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(3) & =500\,{e}^{k\cdot 3} \\ 2\,000 & =500\,{e}^{3k} \\ {e}^{3k} & =\frac{2\,000}{500} \\ {e}^{3k} & =4 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3k}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ 3k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ k & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ k & =0.462\,09…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k≈46%,$ rounded to the nearest percent.
